title: Reservation tradeoffs — 1:1 prep
content:
Purpose / goal:
- Prep for 1:1 with Sam (capacity lead). Walk through concrete tradeoffs for upcoming quarter: commit level vs burst allowance vs autoscale rules. Want to leave with clear ask (target commit) + fallback plan.

Top-line recommendation (starter):
- Commit 120 A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved) + 25% burst capacity via preemptible/spot for spikes.
- Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at 72% avg utilization across pool for 3min, scale-down at <40% for 10min.

Why this combo?
- Predictable baseline for steady jobs (batch evals, nightly index builds).
- Burst covers customer-facing latency spikes and onboarding flurries without overcommitting.

Back-of-envelope numbers (monthly):
- 1 A100-equivalent reserved hour cost = $X (internal rate). 120 GPUs * 24 * 30 = 86,400 reserved GPU-hours.
- If baseline utilization 55% -> billable reserved hours effectively used ~47,520.
- Bursts: assume 2000 spot-hours/month -> incremental cost ~ 2.3% of reserved spend (cheap but less reliable).
- If we undercommit by 30 GPUs, fallback to hosted model pool adds ~30–45% latency penalty on p95 for large requests — risk to SLAs.

Scenarios to propose in meeting:
- Scenario A (conservative): commit 150 GPUs, minimal burst (10%). Good for growth but higher committed spend.
- Scenario B (balanced) [recommended]: commit 120 GPUs + 25% burst. Mid spend, keeps latency tail covered.
- Scenario C (lean): commit 90 GPUs + heavy burst (40%). Lower baseline cost but higher risk of capacity churn and queueing for large embeddings/batch jobs.

Open questions to surface to Sam:
- Are there any upcoming enterprise pilots that require guaranteed single-tenant capacity? If yes, we may need to earmark subset and increase commit.
- Tolerance for monthly variance in committed spend vs ability to shift credits/convert in-quarter?
- Appetite for cross-region reservations (US->EU) to reduce hot-region risk?

Operational concerns / runbook notes (quick checklist):
- Validate current autoscale cooldown windows (prod config key: autoscale.cooldown_ms) — I think it's 300000 (5m) now, propose 600000 for scale-down.
- Exercise prefix/KV cache metrics before committing to aggressive quantization profiles; cache hit rate reduces effective required GPUs.
- Canary plan: reserve extra 10 GPUs for 2 weeks post-rollout to soak real traffic.

Follow-ups I want after the 1:1 (actions to own):
- Sam: decision on commit target + signoff on budget reallocation (due: 2026-03-18)
- Me (Priya): if commit approved, create reservation request ticket and upload capacity calendar; if not, spin detailed scenario C mitigation plan (due: 2026-03-22)
- Evan: validate burst pool cold-start latency numbers and add to the slide (due: 2026-03-14)
- Marco: run 48h spike simulation against current autoscale rules and share p95/p99 metrics (due: 2026-03-16)

Notes to self (prep checklist before meeting):
- Pull last 6 weeks of pool utilization + per-route token distribution.
- Prepare 1 slide with cost delta A/B/C + expected p95 latency impact.
- Have a short fallback phrase: "If commit not approved today, we'll enact controlled throttles + prioritized routing to dedicated-critical models."

Loose brainstorm items (can bring up if time):
- Offer customers "soft reservations" credits that auto-convert to burst capacity for short windows.
- Pilot auto-scaling credits program: dynamically purchase spot capacity in bursts tied to external budget pool.
- Model-aware reservation: pin reserve only for heavy KV-cache models and route lightweight models to mixed-hosted tier.

Random scratch thoughts (not for meeting unless asked):
- Could we set up a 2-week rolling average alert on commit-utilization and automatically trigger finance review if >20% variance?
- If we reserve GPUs across multiple instance families (e.g., A100 + H100), work out equivalence ratio; build simple converter doc.

End of prep. Keep this file as the working scratchpad; will convert to slides if Sam wants numbers live.
summary: 1:1 prep for capacity commit decision: recommend 120 GPUs reserved + 25% burst. Scenarios, B/E numbers, action items and follow-ups.
